FICTIONAL EXERCISE — REFERENCE ONLY. All people, places, organizations, dates, capacities and communications identifiers in Operation Testify are invented. This is a worked authoring example, not a real order, an approved plan, or evidence that any simulated action has occurred.

The fictional Republic of Bellwether has requested assistance after Storm Lyra isolated three communities on Testify Island: Harborhaven, Cedar Vale and Northmere. The island has 18,400 fictional residents; exercise controllers assess 2,400 temporarily displaced people. The area of interest includes the island ferry terminal, municipal water works, district hospital and the mainland relief depot. No real coordinates, current threat reporting or operational frequencies are used.

Exercise day zero is 15 November 2030. The Bellwether Civil Emergency Agency (BCEA) remains the supported authority. Task Force Lantern provides temporary transport, engineering, communications and administrative support. Weather, damage and population figures are planning assumptions until verified within the exercise.

The assigned area consists of the Harborhaven logistics hub, Cedar Vale community center, Northmere school shelter and the roads connecting them. Harborhaven contains the coordination center, municipal warehouse and ferry receiving point. Cedar Vale has a damaged water distribution point and intermittent power. Northmere has restricted road access and requires a separate welfare visit.

Named routes are exercise references: LANTERN is the coastal road, CEDAR is the inland link and NORTH is the final approach to Northmere. A road name does not establish that it is safe or open. Engineering release, civilian consent and weather clearance are separate prerequisites. No geospatial overlay or surveyed route is represented by these narratives.

No armed adversary is part of this scenario. Planning hazards are floodwater, damaged electrical infrastructure, unreliable information, fatigue, traffic congestion and loss of communications. Rumor injects are controlled exercise material and must never be passed off as verified observations.

No surveillance of private communications, interrogation, offensive cyber activity, deception of the public or live weapons activity is authorized by this reference. Any future scenario with a different mission requires its own assumptions and review; do not repurpose these statements as real rules of engagement.

Task Force Lantern is an invented civil-support formation. Its canonical Task Organization contains a headquarters, two relief companies, an engineer detachment, a sustainment company, a medical liaison team, a signal platoon and a civil liaison team. Sub-elements provide transport, supply, maintenance, water-system assessment and public information support. Unit membership and parent relationships are maintained in Task Organization rather than duplicated in this narrative.

The BCEA incident commander determines civil priorities. The district hospital retains clinical decisions; municipal utilities retain authority to return their systems to service. Volunteer organizations remain outside the military command hierarchy.

BCEA chairs the coordination group. The Testify Municipal Council identifies community needs, Harborhaven Hospital coordinates patient referrals, the Testify Water Cooperative owns water infrastructure, and the fictional Northlight Relief Society manages shelter services. A Coastal Transport Office schedules ferries. These civilian bodies are partners, not subordinate units.

Each partner designates one liaison and one alternate. Requests enter a shared request register with a request ID, consent or authority, priority, owner, due time and closure evidence. Public claims about service restoration require confirmation from the responsible civilian operator.

Protect dignity, consent and fair access. Use aggregate shelter and supply counts in the general planning package; do not enter patient records, identity documents, exact home addresses or private contact lists. Provide an accessible help point, translated notices, child safeguarding referral and a confidential complaints path.

The municipal council prioritizes shelter, drinking water and access to health services. Community representatives review whether remote settlements are receiving comparable support. Religious sites, schools, homes and health facilities remain civilian spaces. Assistance is not conditioned on participation in the exercise or provision of unnecessary personal information.

The task force is assembled solely for this fictional exercise. Canonical units and their parentUnitId relationships show the working organization. No Saved ORBAT, personal organization profile or existing operation is altered. The medical and civil liaison elements coordinate with their civilian counterparts without assuming control over them.

Detachments return to their parent administrative organizations after the handover review. A planning relationship is not a statement of legal command authority over any real person or institution.

A1: BCEA has requested the exercise support and named its incident commander. Verify at the opening coordination meeting.
A2: Harborhaven warehouse is structurally safe. The engineer lead must inspect before occupation; use the community-center staging room if it is not released.
A3: Ferry access is available for one relief delivery per exercise day. If canceled, the sustainment lead proposes a revised allocation before dispatch.
A4: Civilian organizations can accept the handover by day four. This is a planning assumption, not a time-driven obligation.
A5: Offline computers and printed control sheets are available if the exercise network fails.
Every assumption has an owner, verification event and consequence. Unverified reports are labeled as such, and phase transition decisions remain conditional.

Task Force Lantern conducts the fictional Operation Testify civil-support exercise on Testify Island from the scheduled H-hour, assisting BCEA to restore access to relief services, coordinate supplies and re-establish reliable information flow, so that civilian agencies can sustain essential support without task-force assistance.

The mission concludes only after the recorded handover criteria are met or the exercise director terminates the exercise. Canonical tasks, objectives and timeline events linked below hold assignments and timing; the narrative provides their shared intent.

Reduce avoidable disruption after the fictional storm while demonstrating that a single authoritative planning dataset can support orders, annexes, matrices and a communications card. Preserve civilian leadership and leave each service with an identified civilian owner. Favor reversible assistance, documented decisions and safe pauses over attempts to meet a clock at any cost.

Phase 1 — Prepare and coordinate: confirm the fictional request, establish liaison, check resources and rehearse stop-work and lost-communications procedures.
Phase 2 — Assess and establish: verify community priorities, inspect proposed facilities, prove communications and release only safe activities.
Phase 3 — Support and stabilize: operate relief points, sustain deliveries, resolve shortfalls and measure fair access.
Phase 4 — Transfer and recover: conduct a joint inventory, transfer open requests, reconcile equipment and capture lessons.

Phases are managed as canonical references, not separate annex-specific calendars. The timeline sets review opportunities; completion criteria govern actual transitions. Unmet prerequisites trigger a documented hold, a named owner and a next review time.

Use UTC for exercise event timestamps; Ordo may display local time according to workstation preferences. H-hour and relative events are maintained in Timeline. All participants may call STOP EXERCISE for an actual safety concern; real emergencies leave the simulation immediately and follow local emergency arrangements.

No live fires, hazardous demonstrations, unapproved flying, real patient movement or offensive cyber activity form part of this example. Exercise channels and callsigns are fictitious labels, not assigned frequencies. Equipment use requires the real operator’s normal authorization outside this reference.

Decision gates: coordination accepted; facility and route safety released; relief service demonstrated; civilian owner accepts handover. At each gate record the evidence, decision, dissent and unresolved actions. A missing report is “not confirmed,” never automatically green.

The package includes every active top-level annex A–Z. O, T, X and Y remain reserved. The conflicting J.1 sample alternative remains omitted in favor of Table D-2 Public Affairs Guidance; its differing source title is retained. Graphics-designated products contain labeled planning briefs, not fabricated maps. Some combat-specific subproducts document non-use and boundaries explicitly.

Use Harborhaven as a single receiving and reconciliation point with separate dispatch queues for Cedar Vale and Northmere. The sustainment company records opening balance, receipts, issues, losses and closing balance by item. Civilian relief supplies remain distinct from task-force consumables. Daily priorities are drinking-water distribution, shelter support, essential transport and equipment readiness.

The exercise planning load is 2,400 relief packs, 12,000 liters of packaged water, 600 blankets and 18 portable power units. These are invented stock quantities, not humanitarian or medical standards. Actual needs and safety requirements would be determined by competent local authorities.

Planning resources: 12 light support vehicles, 8 cargo vehicles, 2 service vehicles, 18 portable power units and 6 water-distribution containers. Vehicle capacities and readiness are controller inputs; no unverified bridge or load limit is assumed. Keep one planned delivery wave in reserve and report any forecast stockout before the next coordination review.

Sign for each transfer using request ID, item, quantity, receiving role, time and discrepancy. Quarantine damaged material. Separate potable-water equipment, food-handling areas, fuel servicing and waste collection under qualified supervision. End each shift with a stock count and maintenance exceptions log.

Fictional planning strength is 216 task-force personnel; the example does not create a real personnel roster. Section leads account for duty status and relief cover without placing sensitive personal data in the OPORD. Staff functions include operations, logistics, engineering, communications, civil liaison, medical liaison and assessment.

Provide shift handover, rest opportunities, welfare access and an accessible way to raise concerns. Record staffing shortfalls as role/quantity/period rather than personal diagnoses. The reference uses role titles instead of inventing individual signatures or approvals.

Harborhaven Hospital is the fictional clinical coordinating authority. The medical liaison team routes aggregate support requests and confirms that referral arrangements are understood; it does not prescribe treatment or certify facilities. Clinical records remain outside this operation.

A real illness or injury takes priority over exercise play. Pause the affected activity, contact the appropriate real emergency service through established local arrangements and notify the exercise director. Exercise casualty injects use visibly fictional identifiers and must not occupy real emergency channels.

BCEA is the supported civilian authority; Task Force Lantern headquarters coordinates its assigned elements. The task-force lead delegates routine coordination to the operations lead and may designate an acting lead in a recorded handover. No real individual is assigned command by this document.

The primary exercise coordination center is Harborhaven Civic Hall; the alternate is Cedar Vale Community Center after safety release. Decision records identify role, timestamp, reason, conditions and review time. Partner agencies retain their own chains of responsibility. The end-of-day meeting resolves priorities and contested resource requests.

Use the authoritative Signal workspace and its linked nets and PACE plans. Annex H and the communications card derive those same facts. Names, membership, exercise channel labels and lost-communications instructions are changed there once; this field does not reproduce the card.

Communications planning demonstrates an offline-first command board, exercise voice coordination, liaison alternatives and logged delivery of critical messages. No encryption keys, passwords, real frequencies or personal contact details appear in this package.

Priority questions are whether each shelter can receive supplies, whether routes have safety release, and which communities have not been contacted.
